basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 2.' and it opens '(Cap. VIII.—Vers. 2.) Et quievit aqua, et revelati sunt fontes abyssi, et cataractae'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. VIII.—Vers. 2.) Et quievit aqua, et revelati sunt fontes abyssi, et cataractae coeli. Pro revelatis fontibus, clausos et obturatos, omnes interpretes transtulerunt. Et pro eo quod sequitur: cessavit aqua super terram, et reliqua, scriptum est, et reversae sunt aquae de terra, euntes et redeuntes (Eccles. I, 7). Nota secundum Ecclesiasten, quod omnes aquae atque torrentes, per occultas venas ad matricem abyssum [Al. abyssi.] revertantur.
